description_summary: 12-month unduplicated student headcounts broken down by enrollment level, sex, and race/ethnicity. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS institution ID (UNITID) and enrollment level (EFFYLEV); the table includes undergraduate and graduate counts, both old and new race/ethnicity categories, and derived combined categories used during the 2008-09 transition to new race/ethnicity reporting.

12-month instructional activity measured by total credit hours and/or contact hours, reported separately for undergraduate and graduate activity. Records are defined by institution (UNITID) and instructional level (EFIALEV); these measures support calculation of 12-month full-time-equivalent enrollment.

Awards and degrees conferred by six-digit CIP program, certificate or degree award level, first or second major, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CIPCODE, MAJORNUM, and AWLEVEL, with counts for total awards and sex and race/ethnicity groups.

Awards in six STEM fields by certificate or degree award level, race/ethnicity, and gender, restricted to first majors. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, STEMCODE, and CMSAWLEV; STEMCODE represents the grouped STEM program fields rather than an individual six-digit CIP program.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Records are uniquely identified by UNITID and EFLEVEL and include total, men’s, and women’s counts overall and by attendance status.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Records are uniquely identified by UNITID and EFALEVEL; the table includes old and new race/ethnicity categories, derived combined categories, and the Two or more races category during the 2009 transition period.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by age category, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Records are uniquely identified by UNITID, EFBAGE, and LSTUDY. Age-specific enrollment is optional for institutions to report in even-numbered years, so 2009 (odd) has data.

Counts of first-time freshmen broken down by state of residence, including counts who graduated from high school the previous year. Records are uniquely identified by UNITID and EFCSTATE. Residence data are optional for institutions to report in odd-numbered years, so 2009 (odd) is an optional reporting year.

Institution-level measures of total entering class, first-year retention rates, and the student-to-faculty ratio; each record is identified by UNITID. Entering-class data are available only for academic-year institutions, all measures apply only to institutions with undergraduate students, and short-program institutions do not have retention data.

Institutional finance records for public institutions using GASB accounting standards, with one record per institution (UNITID). The FY 2009 transition means an institution may have used either the new aligned GASB form or the older unaligned form; F_VER in the FLAGS2009 response file identifies the form and affects the available expense detail, including treatment of operations and maintenance, depreciation, and interest.

Institutional finance records for private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions using FASB accounting standards, with one record per institution (UNITID). FY 2009 was a transition year between the older unaligned FASB form and the new aligned form; F_VER in FLAGS2009 identifies the form, and aligned records can distinguish unrestricted, temporarily restricted, and permanently restricted revenue by source.

Institutional finance records for private for-profit institutions using FASB accounting standards, with one record per institution (UNITID). This form reports revenues by source, expenditures by category, and assets and liabilities for the for-profit population.

Graduation-rate cohort enrollment, completion, and transfer counts broken down by gender and race/ethnicity for four-year and two-year institutions. Records are uniquely defined by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and cohort/graduation-status type (GRTYPE); the four-year records distinguish bachelor’s degree-seeking students from students seeking other degrees or certificates, and 2009 includes old, new, and derived race/ethnicity variables from the reporting transition. Counts completing within 100 percent of normal time are not available by gender and race/ethnicity for two-year institutions.

Graduation-rate cohort enrollment, completion, and transfer counts for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at less-than-two-year institutions, using the 2006 cohort. Institution-level records cover enrollment and completion within 100 or 150 percent of normal time, plus transfer-out status.

Graduation-rate cohort enrollment and bachelor’s completion counts at 200 percent of normal time, using the 2001 cohort for four-year institutions and the 2005 cohort for less-than-four-year institutions. Four-year records are for bachelor’s degree-seeking students and include completion within 100, 150, or 200 percent of normal time; less-than-four-year records cover completion of any degree or certificate at those same milestones.

Staff counts by occupational category, faculty and tenure status, medical school status, and full- or part-time status. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPRECTP, which defines the occupational, tenure, and employment-status combination.

Full- and part-time payroll staff counts by occupational category, race/ethnicity, and gender, covering the broad staff population. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SABDTYPE, which defines occupational category and full- or part-time status. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2009 (odd) has data.

Employees at degree-granting institutions with fewer than 15 full-time employees and at all nondegree-granting institutions, including related administrative offices, broken down by primary function or occupation, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SCNLEVEL, the primary function/occupation. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2009 (odd) has data.

Full-time instruction, research, and public-service staff at degree-granting institutions with at least 15 full-time employees, including related administrative offices, broken down by faculty/tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each row is keyed by UNITID and ARANK, where ARANK combines faculty status and academic rank. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2009 (odd) has data.

Full-time new hires at degree-granting institutions with at least 15 full-time employees, including related administrative offices, broken down by primary occupation, race/ethnicity, and gender; the new-hire period is July 1 through October 31 of the survey year. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SGTYPE, which defines the primary occupation. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2009 (odd) has data.
Counts and salary outlays for full-time nonmedical instructional staff, broken down by gender, academic rank, and contract length. Each row is keyed by UNITID, ARANK, and CONTRACT.
Counts of full-time nonmedical instructional faculty with contracts shorter than 9 months, broken down by gender and academic rank. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK.

Fringe-benefit recipient counts, total expenditures, and average expenditures for full-time nonmedical instructional staff, broken down by contract length and benefit plan type. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and BENTYPE.

Full-time nonmedical instructional staff at 4-year institutions, broken down by faculty status, contract length, gender, and academic rank. Rows are identified by UNITID, CONTRACT, and ARANK; faculty status categories include tenured, tenure-track, non-tenure-track/no-tenure-system, and without faculty status.

Response and applicability status by institution and survey component, including response, imputation, nonresponse, parent/child or multi-campus reporting, and revised-data indicators. The record grain is one institution–survey-component combination.

Directory information for each institution, including name, address, contact and web links, active status, Title IV participation, and institution-level characteristics such as control, level, highest award offered, and Carnegie classification. The record grain is one institution.

Institution-level educational offerings, award levels, control and affiliations, special learning opportunities, admissions, applicants, and test scores. Admissions, applicant, and test-score fields are available only for institutions that do not have an open-admission policy; the record grain is one institution.

Academic-year student charges for institutions with primarily credit-hour academic programs using a semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or other academic calendar. It contains full-time and part-time undergraduate and graduate tuition and required fees, full-time first-time undergraduate price-of-attendance components, and charges for doctoral professional-practice students; first-professional reporting was eliminated in 2009-10, and typical charges for the listed doctoral professional-practice fields were not collected in this first mandatory year. The record grain is one institution, with charges distinguished by student level and attendance status.

Program-length charges for institutions using clock hours or primarily occupational credit-hour programs. The institution-level record includes the number of programs, price of attendance for entering students in the largest program, and tuition, fees, and books-and-supplies amounts for up to five additional programs; program-specific charge slots distinguish the largest and additional programs.
The institution’s mission statement or the web address where it is available. The record grain is one institution.

Student financial aid recipient counts and total and average aid amounts, broken down by student population and aid source/type. It has separate rows for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates—covering federal, Pell, other federal, state/local, institutional grants, and federal and nonfederal loans—and for all undergraduates—covering total grants, Pell grants, and federal loans.

Average net price and the underlying financial-aid amounts for two full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate groups: students receiving grant or scholarship aid and students receiving Title IV federal aid. For public institutions, both groups are limited to students paying in-district or in-state tuition; net-price data are available for 2006-07 through 2008-09 for the grant/scholarship group, but only 2008-09 for the Title IV group.
